description: Scheduled hardening suite: every lane the main profile runs, plus mutation testing at concurrency 8, the k6 public-route load check, a database concurrency stress lane, and the full ZAP scan.
notes: Command lists are transcribed from .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/nightly.yml as they stand today; where a hosted step is a GitHub Action or an inline shell block rather than a command, the transcription is recorded in that lane's notes.

baselineEnv is ci.yml's workflow-level env block verbatim, plus CI=1 so forbidOnly, failOnFlakyTests and retries behave as they do hosted. Browser lanes explicitly override PLAYWRIGHT_NODE_HEAP_MB to 12288 MiB; hosted retains its 8192 MiB default.

The three entropy-bearing values ci.yml sets inline (CUSTOMER_SESSION_SECRET, CUSTOMER_PHONE_HMAC_SECRET, CUSTOMER_PHONE_ENCRYPTION_KEY) are absent from baselineEnv on purpose and come from the profile-level strict-fixtures runtime source, so no secret-shaped literal is committed to this file. The values it mints are equal to or stronger than the hosted ones on every rule scripts/check-env.mjs enforces.

Values that only exist at run time - the anon and service-role keys `supabase status -o env` prints, the generated VAPID pair, the auth-hook signing fixture - are referenced by runtime source id, never inlined. The source definitions live in config/local-ci-contract.json under runtimeEnv.
Env precedence is baselineEnv, then baselineRuntimeEnv, then the lane's runtimeEnv, then the lane's literal env.

No lane in any profile writes or compares a pixel baseline: every Playwright invocation carries both --grep-invert @visual and --ignore-snapshots, and no command contains -u, --update-snapshots or test:visual. Visual regression stays GitHub-hosted on x64.
Lanes run at up to agent.maxConcurrentLanes at once; lanes sharing a concurrencyGroup are serialised against each other.

The first ten lanes are the main profile's lanes unchanged; the last four are the nightly-only additions. A contract test asserts the prefix relationship so nightly can never quietly drop a merge-path lane.

nightly.yml's cross-browser job is not reproduced as a separate lane: it runs the same `pnpm test:e2e -- --project=... --grep-invert @visual --shard=...` command as ci.yml's e2e tier, which the four e2e lanes above already cover for all four projects.
nightly.yml's load-race job is absent because it requires repository secrets, which cannot reach this plane; it stays hosted.
zap-full is declared arch x64-only and is skipped and recorded as pinned-hosted on the ARM64 plane.

Every lane installs the commit's own dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` before it runs any command that needs them, which is the transcription of .github/actions/setup. A job container mounts a bare git worktree at container.workspacePath and nothing else, so without it `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:coverage`, every Next.js build and every Playwright invocation fail immediately on a missing dependency tree. --frozen-lockfile is the half that makes it a check rather than a convenience: a commit whose pnpm-lock.yaml disagrees with its package.json fails the lane instead of quietly resolving some other tree. The image bakes a warm pnpm STORE rather than a node_modules (ops/local-ci/image/Dockerfile runs `pnpm fetch`), so the install is served from cache across runs and can still never answer with a stale dependency tree; and because every lane of a run shares one worktree and the lanes run in sequence, only the first lane of a run pays for the resolution. It is commands[0] everywhere except db-stress, where agent/runner.mjs resolves a per-lane runtimeEnv source immediately after commands[0] and that slot therefore has to stay `supabase start`.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from .github/workflows/ci.yml's fast job, in order. The unit suite runs exactly once, with coverage thresholds enforced.

lanes.title: Quality lane (hygiene sweeps)
lanes.notes: The seven maintainability sweeps from ci.yml's quality job, in order. The PDF proof that shares that hosted job lives in the print-kit lane here, because its dependency set (poppler, ImageMagick, two Python wheels, a browser and a running dev server) is disjoint from the sweeps and would otherwise be installed for a lane that never uses it. `pnpm docs:check` regenerates docs/api/README.md and then runs `git diff --exit-code`, so this lane requires the full-history checkout that agent.gitFetchDepth 0 provides; a shallow clone reports a spurious diff.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from the last two steps of ci.yml's quality job. `pnpm posters:verify-pdfs` is the pdf-lib vector geometry proof and needs no server; `pnpm posters:verify-production-pdfs` renders the exact Playwright production bundle (duplex posters, tents, cards and plates) against a live preview server, so the release gate cannot pass against a stand-in PDF path. ci.yml expresses the server as an inline shell block that backgrounds `pnpm exec next dev --webpack -H 127.0.0.1`, polls /dev/poster-preview?template=seal up to 60 times at one-second intervals, dumps the log and exits 1 if it never answers, and kills the process on EXIT. That is declared here as a backgroundService with startAfter 1 rather than transcribed as a heredoc, so the agent owns the lifecycle and the readiness contract is machine-readable. concurrencyGroup http-127.0.0.1-3000 keeps this lane, the nightly load lane and the nightly zap-full lane off each other's port. Inserting the install shifts every later command by one, so this lane's backgroundService.startAfter - the index in `commands` after which the service starts - moves with it and the server still comes up after the command it depends on.

lanes.title: Functional E2E (chromium)

systemDependencies.name: playwright-chromium
systemDependencies.note: Installed by `pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps` at image build time, pinned to the @playwright/test version in pnpm-lock.yaml.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from .github/workflows/ci.yml's e2e job (`pnpm test:e2e -- --project="${{ matrix.project }}" ...`). Sharded 8 ways, one Playwright invocation per shard, each with its own fresh webpack dev server. Sharding here buys memory, not parallelism: nightly.yml records that an UNSHARDED run against one dev server dies with "FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit - JavaScript heap out of memory" after roughly 154 tests (run 30196429475, chromium 13 failed / 141 passed), after which every navigation fails with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. 1/8 of a project is about 28 functional tests per dev server, five times inside that recorded failure point, and it is the denominator the hosted a11y tier already runs green. The hosted e2e denominator of 32 is not copied because hosted sharding also buys 32-way runner parallelism that a single-machine plane does not have: 32 shards x 4 projects would be 128 sequential dev-server boots and would blow the 75-minute local budget on process startup alone. Carries --grep-invert @visual and --ignore-snapshots so this lane can neither read nor write a pixel baseline. Playwright encodes only process.platform in the {platform} snapshot token, so the blessed x86-64 `-linux` PNGs resolve identically on ARM64; visual regression therefore stays on the GitHub-hosted x64 `visual` / `visual-gate` jobs in ci.yml, which cutover step 1 does not touch. PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS "1" and the CUSTOMER_DEV_OTP_CODE "424242" fixture are carried exactly where ci.yml carries them: under two workers the webpack dev server intermittently 500s mid-suite and failOnFlakyTests turns any recovery into a red run. PLAYWRIGHT_REGULAR_CHROMIUM "1" is job-level env on the hosted lane and is carried on every project for the same reason. PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, PLAYWRIGHT_NEXT_DIST_DIR and PLAYWRIGHT_NODE_HEAP_MB deliberately differ from hosted. The 12288 MiB heap override, versus the hosted 8192 MiB default, gives larger local shards headroom within the 32 GiB job container. For URL and dist isolation: every hosted shard owns a whole runner, so all of them use the 127.0.0.1:3146 default and the shared .next-e2e directory. Here up to agent.maxConcurrentLanes lanes share one machine, so each lane is given its own dev-server port (3146) and its own Next dist directory. Every e2e spec and helper reads process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL with 3146 only as a fallback, and scripts/run-playwright.mjs treats a caller-supplied PLAYWRIGHT_NEXT_DIST_DIR as caller-owned, so the agent removes it after the lane.

lanes.title: DB behavioral moat

systemDependencies.name: supabase-cli
systemDependencies.note: Same version ci.yml and production-database.yml pin through supabase/setup-cli.

systemDependencies.name: docker-engine
systemDependencies.note: Runs inside the job container (container.dockerInDocker); the host Docker socket is never mounted.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from ci.yml's db job. `supabase start` and `supabase stop --no-backup` wrap `pnpm db:seed` and `pnpm test:db`; the stop is a teardownCommand rather than a command because ci.yml runs it under `if: always()`, and teardownCommands run whether the lane passed or failed. The two env values are the exact ones ci.yml sets: the 3147 auth-hook URI on host.docker.internal, and the local Supabase Postgres URL that tests/db/helpers/db-target.mjs validates as local before any test module can open a client. This lane deliberately does NOT use the supabase-local runtime source: ci.yml's db job reaches Postgres directly over SUPABASE_DB_URL and never reads `supabase status`, so adding minted anon and service-role keys here would be a divergence, not a fix. The nightly db-stress lane does need them, and declares them. `pnpm test:db` is already --test-concurrency=1, so the concurrencyGroup exists for the local Supabase ports (54321/54322), not for the suite. SUPABASE_DB_URL stays on loopback, and has to: tests/db/helpers/db-target.mjs refuses any SUPABASE_DB_URL whose hostname is not 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1, so no environment edit can aim the database tier at a real database. For daemon-backed lanes, agent/container.mjs waits for the job-private sidecar's Docker API, then shares that sidecar's network namespace with the unprivileged job container. Docker and nested Supabase services are reachable on loopback without sharing the VM network or mounting its Docker socket.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from nightly.yml's mutation job, with `--concurrency 8` added. The command runner first runs tests that directly exercise the eight mutation targets. Every survivor then runs the complete unit suite; only already detected mutants exit early. The full mutation scope, score thresholds and 75-minute local lane budget remain required. Chromium remains required because the full unit suite includes browser-backed PDF tests. A focused sample is diagnostic only; qualification requires all mutants at concurrency eight within budget.

systemDependencies.note: nightly.yml installs it through grafana/setup-k6-action with no version input, so the action's own default floats. lanes.notes: Transcribed from nightly.yml's load job. `pnpm build`, then `pnpm start` backgrounded with its output captured, then a 60-attempt two-second curl readiness loop that dumps the log and exits 1 on failure, then `k6 run tests/load/public-routes.js` with BASE_URL pointing at the started server. The server is declared as a backgroundService with startAfter 1 so it comes up after the build and is torn down by the agent. nightly.yml's load-race job is deliberately absent from this profile: it reads secrets.STAMP_RACE_AUTH_TOKEN and vars.STAMP_RACE_URL, and a repository secret cannot reach this plane at all (see the contract's hostSecretsPolicy). It stays hosted. Inserting the install shifts every later command by one, so this lane's backgroundService.startAfter - the index in `commands` after which the service starts - moves with it and the server still comes up after the command it depends on.

lanes.notes: The one nightly lane with no hosted precedent to transcribe: nightly.yml has no database job at all, so this is new surface and is declared advisory-by-position (nothing depends on it) rather than by continueOnError. `pnpm db:reseed:stress` is scripts/seed-stress.mjs --clean --count 10000, and `pnpm perf:stress` then benchmarks the same Supabase reads the merchant app issues, including the concurrent-claim RPC paths the tests/db lane only proves for correctness at --test-concurrency=1. SUPABASE_DB_URL stays on loopback, and has to: tests/db/helpers/db-target.mjs refuses any SUPABASE_DB_URL whose hostname is not 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1, so no environment edit can aim the database tier at a real database. Docker and nested Supabase services are reachable on loopback without sharing the VM network or mounting its Docker socket.

lanes.title: ZAP full scan
commands: docker run --rm --network host -v "$PWD:/zap/wrk:rw" ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable zap-full-scan.py -t http://127.0.0.1:3000 -c .zap/rules.tsv

systemDependencies.name: docker-engine
systemDependencies.note: Runs inside the job container (container.dockerInDocker); the host Docker socket is never mounted.

systemDependencies.name: zaproxy-image
systemDependencies.note: The image behind zaproxy/action-full-scan. Published for linux/amd64; there is no arm64 stable tag, which is the whole reason this lane is arch x64-only.

lanes.notes: Transcribed from nightly.yml's zap-full job: `pnpm build`, `pnpm start` backgrounded, the 60-attempt two-second readiness loop, then zaproxy/action-full-scan@v0.13.0 against http://127.0.0.1:3000 with .zap/rules.tsv and issue writing off. A GitHub Action is not a command, so it is expressed here as the equivalent `docker run` of the image the action wraps, with the workspace mounted at /zap/wrk so the relative rules path resolves the same way. arch is x64-only: the ZAP stable image is linux/amd64. On the ARM64 plane the agent must skip this lane and record it as pinned-hosted rather than emulating it - qemu-emulated ZAP would produce timing-dependent findings that are neither reproducible nor comparable to the hosted result. Flipping this field to `any` is the single change needed if an arm64 ZAP image is ever adopted, and no other structure has to be invented for it. Inserting the install shifts every later command by one, so this lane's backgroundService.startAfter - the index in `commands` after which the service starts - moves with it and the server still comes up after the command it depends on.
